name: Herod Agrippa
charge: Accepting worship due to God alone
summary: Arrayed in royal robes, the king gave an oration and the crowd shouted that his was the voice of a god, not a man. He accepted the acclaim. The judgment was immediate and public.
offense: The sin was not the speech but the silence after it: he took to himself the honor owed to God, receiving worship he should have refused as Paul and Barnabas had refused it at Lystra.
judgment: Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him because he gave not God the glory; he was eaten of worms and died. The contrast follows at once: but the word of God grew and multiplied.

taught.title: Isaiah 42: My Servant and the Light of the Gentiles

lawsResolved.text: I am the LORD your God, you shall have no other gods besides me.

text.text: And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them.
And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.
And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.
I am the Lord: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.
Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
